claims.text: A Cu substrate typically has a native oxide layer.
The native oxide layer can hinder direct adhesion of an HEA coating to Cu.
A thin Ni interlayer can be deposited between the Cu substrate and the HEA coating.
A Ni interlayer will improve the adhesion of a wear-resistant HEA coating to a Cu substrate.
A Ni interlayer enhances wettability at the Cu–HEA interface.
A Ni interlayer reduces interfacial-energy mismatch between Cu and the HEA coating.
Nickel has excellent wettability with copper.
Nickel can form graded metallurgical bonds with HEAs.
The Ni interlayer accommodates thermal-expansion differences between the substrate and coating.
Reduction of interfacial-energy mismatch and accommodation of thermal-expansion differences improve mechanical interlocking at the interface.
Reduction of interfacial-energy mismatch and accommodation of thermal-expansion differences improve chemical adhesion at the interface.
Direct deposition of an HEA coating on Cu typically produces poor wettability.
Direct deposition of an HEA coating on Cu typically produces weak interfacial bonding.
Compared with direct HEA deposition on Cu, use of a Ni interlayer will produce a more durable interface.
Compared with direct HEA deposition on Cu, use of a Ni interlayer will produce a more wear-resistant surface.
The benefit of the Ni interlayer may be limited under extremely aggressive wear conditions.
The benefit of the Ni interlayer may be limited at temperatures that exceed the graded interface's ability to accommodate thermal-expansion differences.
